title: How many times larger is one power than another?
description: Two comparisons are made with powers of four: sixteen thousand three hundred and eighty four against one thousand and twenty four, and four squared against four to the power negative two. Keeko doubts what happens when a negative exponent is taken away.
teaching_notes: One idea: how many times larger one power is than another is found by dividing, which takes the exponents away. Watch for students who treat taking away a negative exponent as taking away a positive one.

source: Show that 16384 is 16 times 1024, and find how many times larger 4² is than 4 to the power −2.
video_script.why: A learner compares two powers of one base by dividing them and taking the exponents away, even when an exponent is negative.
video_script.substitution: the book's own comparison of powers of four
video_script.anchor: two comparisons written on the board, one with big numbers and one with powers of four
video_script.wrong_answer: four to the power zero, which is one
video_script.wrong_move: takes away the exponent negative two as if it were two, giving zero
video_script.payoff_line: Taking away a negative exponent is the same as adding

final_answer.value: 16384 is 16 times 1024; 4² is 4⁴, which is 256, times 4 to the power −2
final_answer.spoken: sixteen thousand three hundred and eighty four is sixteen times one thousand and twenty four; four squared is four to the power four, which is two hundred and fifty six, times four to the power negative two

video_script.design: One idea: times larger means divide, and dividing takes the exponents away. Wrong idea: two take away negative two is zero. The 256 stays hidden until the answer, where a number check confirms it.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; two comparisons on the board with a question mark

marks.one: 16384 and 1024 are written side by side with a link between them
marks.two: 4^2 and 4^-2 are written side by side with a link between them
marks.ask: a question mark glows beside both links

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This question is from your book.
<bookmark mark='one'/>Show that sixteen thousand three hundred and eighty four is sixteen times one thousand and twenty four.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Then find how many times larger four squared is than four to the power negative two.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How would you compare them?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: how many times larger = bigger / smaller; same base: take the exponents away

marks.times: the words how many times larger become bigger divided by smaller
marks.rule: a rule card opens: same base, divide, take the exponents away

narration: <bookmark mark='times'/>To find how many times larger one number is, we divide the bigger by the smaller.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>For powers of one base, dividing takes the exponents away.

marks.given: the two pairs are written in a row

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, sixteen thousand three hundred and eighty four and one thousand and twenty four. Also four squared and four to the power negative two.

beats.on_screen: To find: how many times larger each first number is

marks.find: the words how many times larger are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find how many times larger the first number is in each pair.
<bookmark mark='big'/>Step one, write both as powers of four. Sixteen thousand three hundred and eighty four is four to the power seven.
<bookmark mark='small'/>One thousand and twenty four is four to the power five.

marks.chk: 4^2 = 16 and 16384 / 1024 = 16 are written side by side

narration: <bookmark mark='div'/>Step two, divide the bigger by the smaller. Seven take away five is two, so we get four squared.
<bookmark mark='chk'/>Four squared is sixteen. Dividing the big numbers also gives sixteen, so the first part is shown.
<bookmark mark='div'/>Step three, divide four squared by four to the power negative two. Two take away negative two is the exponent.
<bookmark mark='add'/>Taking away a negative is adding, so two plus two is four.

marks.pay: the minus sign before the bracket with -2 is boxed
marks.two: 4^2 = 4^4 = 256 x 4^-2 is written with the 4^4 boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='pay'/>Taking away a negative exponent is the same as adding.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>Sixteen thousand three hundred and eighty four is sixteen times one thousand and twenty four.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Four squared is four to the power four. That is two hundred and fifty six times four to the power negative two.
<bookmark mark='chk'/>Check, four to the power negative two is one over sixteen. Sixteen divided by one over sixteen is sixteen times sixteen, which is two hundred and fifty six.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble: 2 - (-2) = 0, so 4^0 = 1, struck out; 4^-2 = 1/16 beside it

marks.all: the bubble is struck out and 2 + 2 = 4 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks two take away negative two is zero. The answer would be four to the power zero, which is one.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But four squared is sixteen, and four to the power negative two is only one over sixteen. Sixteen is far larger, so it cannot be one.
<bookmark mark='all'/>Taking away negative two is adding two, so two plus two is four.
